archetype.name: Point Guard (Improviser in reserve)
archetype.definition: This season Mahomes is a quick-game distributor who wins underneath and in the intermediate middle, gets the ball out before pressure lands, and keeps his off-script playmaking as a fallback rather than the plan.

report.headline: A shorter, safer Mahomes: the efficiency is back, but the deep ball isn't.
report.take:
The 2026 version of Mahomes plays very differently from the one who built the reputation. His aggressiveness (throws into tight windows) is 6.9%, down 6.4 points from last year and lower than any season in his career log. His intended air yards sit at 6.09 and he throws 2.41 yards short of the sticks on average. This is a quick-game offense. He distributes the ball to Travis Kelce, Xavier Worthy, Kenneth Walker III, Rashee Rice and Noah Gray, and the team passes more than situation predicts (third in pass rate over expected). The trade is working. His 7.74 yards per attempt is better than any of his last three seasons, and his completion rate over expected has climbed back to 1.52 after a 0.3 year.

The biggest single change is what happens when the pocket collapses. In 2024 and 2025 he took sacks on more than a quarter of his pressures and ranked 20th and 28th. This year that pressure-to-sack rate is 16.3%, fourth best, and his overall sack rate of 3.7% ranks fifth against a league average of 6.9%. That is a return to his 2019-2022 range. With a time to throw of 2.74, it reads as a deliberate design change, not luck. The cost shows up in his legs: rushing is down to 11 yards a game from 30.1. He scrambles on only 5.1% of dropbacks, though those scrambles have been productive.

The efficiency lives in two places. On short throws he is solid. On intermediate throws (10-19 air yards) he is exceptional: 0.684 EPA per attempt on 34 throws with a 7.3 CPOE. Past 20 yards, the deep game has been a dead zone. On 24 attempts he has completed 29.2%, with a -9.7 CPOE, two of his four interceptions and no touchdowns. Week 4 at Las Vegas, his most aggressive game, was also his sloppiest, with a 25.9% bad-throw rate. The target tree explains part of it. Kelce and Gray have been worth a combined fortune per target, while Worthy, nominally the vertical receiver, has been below zero on 41 targets.

The last three weeks dipped to 0.07 EPA per dropback and a 2.9% TD rate. The cause is mostly the schedule: the Chargers and Seahawks rank eighth and fifth in defensive EPA, and Seattle held the offense to three points. The 10.8 EPA bounce-back at Denver, against an 11th-ranked defense, says the floor is intact. Overall he looks like a top-15 efficiency quarterback with a top-5 sack profile, not the league's best. That ceiling probably stays capped unless the deep ball starts landing.

strengths.title: Intermediate middle is a cheat code
strengths.body: Throws of 10-19 air yards are producing a huge EPA rate with a strong completion rate over expected. This is the window where his processing and anticipation still separate him. The sample is only 34 attempts, so the rate will come down. Still, the skill is consistent with his career and should remain a plus.

strengths.title: Pressure no longer turns into sacks
strengths.body: After two years of absorbing sacks on more than a quarter of pressures, he is back among the league's best at getting rid of the ball. A quicker, shorter passing structure drives it, so it should hold as long as the design does. That keeps drives alive and is a big reason his adjusted net yards per dropback beats the league by a full yard.

strengths.title: Kelce and the tight ends
strengths.body: Kelce leads the team in targets and has been worth more than half a point per target. Gray has been even better on a smaller sample. The tight-end room is where his short and intermediate game cashes in, and with Rice adding positive value it gives him a reliable core.

concerns.title: Deep passing has disappeared
concerns.body: His completion rate past 20 air yards is under 30%, with a sharply negative CPOE and two interceptions. Deep throws have not added any value, and Worthy's negative EPA on heavy volume suggests a connection problem more than bad luck. On 24 attempts this could rebound. Without it, his ceiling games will be rare.

concerns.title: Third downs pay the quick-game tax
concerns.body: Throwing short of the sticks shows up on third down. He converts barely a third of the time, with a below-average CPOE and five of his nine sacks. This is the price of the conservative structure rather than a skill decline. It will persist as long as the air yards stay this low.

concerns.title: Red-zone TDs outrunning the process
concerns.body: Eleven of his 12 passing TDs came in the red zone, on a CPOE of 12.6 that will not hold. Red-zone EPA per play is modest, which suggests the touchdown count is ahead of the underlying efficiency. The recent TD-rate dip is partly that regression already arriving.

trend.note: Strong in weeks 2-3, then a two-game slide against the fifth- and eighth-ranked defenses. The worst was a -6.0 EPA game at Seattle, followed by a sharp 10.8 EPA rebound at Denver. The game-to-game swings track opponent quality more than any decline.

nextGame.headline: The Jets' soft underbelly is exactly where he lives.
nextGame.body:
This sets up well for his 2026 profile. The Jets rank 28th in pass defense EPA and 31st against short passes, which is the zone he feeds all game. Their run defense is good (seventh in rush EPA), so the offense has every reason to lean on its pass-first tendency. The Book has the Chiefs at -9.5 with a 46.5 total, which implies a comfortable script. Opposing quarterbacks have not piled up yardage against New York, but touchdowns have come at an above-average clip. A big lead could trim his fourth-quarter volume.

Availability tilts his way. The Jets' sack rate ranks eighth, but they are missing pieces of the front. Starting linebacker David Bailey (81% of snaps) is out, rotational edge Joseph Ossai is out, and DT T'Vondre Sweat is on injured reserve. That should thin the pressure he has been so good at defusing anyway. The Chiefs have no offensive players on the injury report. On the other side, Breece Hall is reported good to go. That helps New York sustain drives and could keep the game closer than the spread.

keyMatchups.title: Quick game vs. a leaky short defense
keyMatchups.body: New York gives up a lot of EPA on short throws, and his short attempts have been steady positive value. This is the cleanest path to an efficient day. Expect heavy volume to Kelce and the backs underneath.

keyMatchups.title: Depleted Jets pass rush
keyMatchups.body: The Jets get home often by sack rate, but three regulars from the front are unavailable. His low pressure-to-sack rate already blunts rushes. A thinner rotation should leave the pocket cleaner than their numbers suggest.

keyMatchups.title: Jets have stifled WR1s
keyMatchups.body: New York has held opposing top receivers well under their averages. That leans against Worthy, already the weak link in his target tree. It argues for the ball flowing to tight ends and Rice.

nextGame.watch: Whether he takes a few real deep shots against a vulnerable secondary, or stays in the dink-and-dunk structure even with an edge.

restOfSeason.body:
The parts of this season built on structure should hold: the low sack rate, the completion gains, the steady short and intermediate efficiency and the pass-leaning game plans. That points to roughly 240-275 passing yards most weeks and EPA per dropback around the league's top-15 tier. The red-zone touchdown rate is the soft spot. Expect closer to 1.4-1.9 passing TDs a game than the early-season pace, since the recent drop is already showing that regression.

Upside depends on the deep ball. Twenty-four attempts is a small sample, and he has historically been a far better downfield thrower than this. A modest rebound there, or Worthy turning volume into value, would lift his ceiling. Rushing looks like a lower-volume part of his game now, so the fantasy floor relies on passing.

confidence.note: Seven games, but the stylistic shift is consistent. Deep and red-zone splits rest on small samples.
